analysis:
Both units are head-text excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 6531-7388). This is documentation only; no code, configuration, key handling or authorization logic is changed. The patch excerpt shows additions about served-scope speed records (`serving`, `tensorAssistant`), a `--layer-stride` option for `tp-check gemma`, and other doc edits. All are descriptive.

Security-relevant claims I read against the threat model:
- Qwen media transport (lines 6623-6695): encoded media goes only to rank 0 and the owner, and rank 1 gets metadata only. Identities and patch digests are re-verified, and prefix reuse is disabled for media ingress (7260-7261). This is consistent with T-041, which expects prefix scope to include the media fingerprint, so cross-tenant leakage is not widened.
- Prefix depth and SSD tier (7221-7238): the text keeps per-request partitions and SSD records. It says the 'balanced' SSD records keep older rows approximate. No change to HMAC naming, TTL or at-rest crypto is described. T-041 and SEC-035 posture is unchanged by prose.
- Sealed collectives (FP32 sums, load-agreement binding of wire versions, fail-closed on non-finite logits) are described as unchanged in behavior, and ranks on different protocols refuse each other at load.
- Build-ahead is stated as not on in the product (`buildsAhead` false).
- Diagnostic environment variables such as `DARKBLOOM_QWEN_TP_PREFILL_STRIDE` and `MLX_QMM_STEEL_TILE` are described as forwarded only by `pair-check`, with installed workers using defaults. No new local attack surface is described.
- Capability/grant text (7324-7343, 7372-7387) says pair serving requires grants, the coordinator holds members without a grant to single-Mac requirements, and media registration is checked against READY. These are consistent with the TB-011 authorization separation.

I have no source for the referenced Swift code, so I cannot verify that the doc matches implementation; that is a coverage limit, not a finding. No regression or new attack surface is identified.
